Cels ex Hoffmanns. |''Arbutus serratifolia'' Salisb. |''Arbutus turbinata'' Pers. ex Rchb. }} }} '''''Arbutus unedo''''', commonly known as '''strawberry tree''', also called '''madrone''', is an evergreen shrub or small tree in the family [[Ericaceae]], native to the [[Mediterranean Basin]] and [[Western Europe]]. The tree is well known for its fruits, the '''arbutus berry''', which bear some resemblance to the [[strawberry]], hence the common name strawberry tree.{{Cite web|url=https://www.atlasobscura.com/foods/strawberry-tree-fruit|title=Fruits & Vegetables: Strawberry Tree Fruit|website=Atlas Obscura|last=Rydelek|first=Jared |date=2014|access-date=23 July 2021}}{{Cite web|title=Arbutus unedo {{!}} strawberry tree|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/1473/Arbutus-unedo/Details |access-date=23 July 2021|website=RHS Gardening|publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society}}{{Cite web|title=Arbutus unedo|url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279932 |access-date=23 July 2021|website=Plant Finder|publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden}} However, it is not closely related to true [[strawberry|strawberries]] of the genus ''Fragaria''. Its presence in Ireland also lends it the name '''Irish strawberry tree''', or '''cain''', or '''cane apple''' (from the Irish name for the tree, {{Lang|ga|caithne}}{{cite web|url=http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/cane+apple|title=cane apple|website=Merriam-Webster Dictionary}}), or sometimes '''[[Killarney]] strawberry tree'''. The strawberry tree is the [[national tree]] of [[Italy]] because of its green leaves, its white flowers and its red berries, colors that recall the [[Italian flag]].{{cite web|url=http://www.altovastese.it/cultura/il-corbezzolo-simbolo-unita-italia-specie-che-resiste-agli-incendi/|title= Il corbezzolo simbolo dell'Unità d'Italia. Una specie che resiste agli incendi|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130424020359/http://www.altovastese.it/cultura/il-corbezzolo-simbolo-unita-italia-specie-che-resiste-agli-incendi/ |url-status=live|archive-date=24 April 2013|date= 3 October 2011|language=it |access-date=25 January 2016|website= Altovastese}} The flower of the strawberry tree is the [[national flower]] of Italy.{{cite web|url=https://www.msn.com/it-it/notizie/mondo/qual-%C3%A8-il-fiore-nazionale-dei-paesi-del-mondo/ss-AA1eWqXE#image=25|title=Il fiore nazionale dell'Italia (e quello degli altri Paesi del mondo)|website=[[MSN]] |access-date=26 August 2024|language=it}} ==Taxonomy== ''Arbutus unedo'' was one of the many species described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in Volume One of his landmark 1753 work ''[[Species Plantarum]]'', giving it the name it still bears today.{{cite book | author=Linnaeus, Carl | author-link=Carl Linnaeus| title=Species Plantarum| publisher=Laurentii Salvii|location=Holmiae (Stockholm), Sweden | year=1753|volume = Tomus I | page=395|quote=caule erecto, foliis glabris serratis, baccis polyspermis|url=http://www.botanicus.org/title/b12069590|language=la}} A study published in 2001 which analyzed [[ribosomal DNA]] from ''Arbutus'' and related genera found ''Arbutus'' to be [[paraphyletic]], and ''A. unedo'' to be closely related to the other [[Mediterranean Basin]] species such as ''[[Arbutus andrachne|A. andrachne]]'' and ''[[Arbutus canariensis|A. canariensis]]'' and not to the western North American members of the genus.{{cite journal|author1=Hileman, Lena C. |author2=Vasey, Michael C. |author3=Parker, V. Thomas |year= 2001|title=Phylogeny and Biogeography of the Arbutoideae (Ericaceae): Implications for the Madrean-Tethyan Hypothesis|journal=Systematic Botany|volume=26|issue=1|pages=131–143 |jstor=2666660 |doi=10.1043/0363-6445-26.1.131|doi-broken-date=11 July 2025 |s2cid=44225779 |url=http://userwww.sfsu.edu/parker/pages/respubs/HilemanEtAl2001.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200714220531/http://userwww.sfsu.edu/parker/pages/respubs/HilemanEtAl2001.pdf |archive-date=14 July 2020 }} ''Arbutus unedo'' and ''A. andrachne'' hybridise naturally where their ranges overlap; the [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrid]] has been named ''Arbutus'' × ''andrachnoides'' (syn. ''A. ''× ''hybrida'', or ''A. andrachne'' × ''unedo''),{{Cite journal|last1=Bertsouklis|first1=Konstantinos Fotios|last2=Papafotiou|first2=Maria|date=2016-12-14|title=Morphometric and Molecular Analysis of the Three Arbutus Species of Greece|url=https://www.notulaebotanicae.ro/index.php/nbha/article/view/10572|journal=Notulae Botanicae Horti Agrobotanici Cluj-Napoca|volume=44|issue=2|pages=423–430|doi=10.15835/nbha44210572|issn=1842-4309|doi-access=free}} inheriting traits of both parent species, although fruits are not usually borne freely, and as a hybrid is unlikely to breed true from seed. It is sold in California as Arbutus x Marina named for a district in San Francisco where it was hybridized.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}} ==Description== [[File:Arbutus_unedo_fruit_close-up.jpg|frameless|right|alt=Fruit]] [[Image:Maginje na Koločepu.JPG|frameless|right|alt=Ripe and unripe fruits and flowers]] [[File:Badaia_-_Barranco_de_los_Goros_-_Madroño_02.jpg|frameless|right|alt=Flowers]] [[File:Strawberry tree berry.jpg|frameless|right|alt=Cut fruit]] [[File:Arbutus unedo_coupe_MHNT.jpg|frameless|right|alt=Cross section of wood]] ''Arbutus unedo'' grows to {{convert|4|-|7|m|abbr=on}} tall,{{cite web |title=A. unedo |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/04_074_07_Arbutus.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=27 November 2021}} rarely up to {{convert|15|m|ft|round=5|abbr=on}}, with a trunk diameter of up to {{convert|80|cm|in|0|abbr=on}}.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}} It grows in [[hardiness zone]]s 7–10.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}} The leaves are green and glossy on the upper side, dull on the underside, {{convert|8|–|10|cm|in|round=0.5|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|3|–|4|cm|in|frac=2|abbr=on}} broad, [[Lauraceae|laurel-like]] and with a serrated or [[serrulate]]d margin. The [[plant sexuality|hermaphrodite]]{{Citation needed|date=November 2021}} flowers are white (yellow when [[desiccation|desiccated]]), bell-shaped, {{convert|7|-|8|mm|in|frac=16|abbr=on}} in diameter, and flower from a reddish hanging panicle in autumn. They are pollinated by bees, and have a mild sweet scent.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}} Twigs are reddish-brown and abundantly foliose, and often have small hairs. The fruit is a red berry, {{convert|7|-|20|mm|in|frac=16|abbr=on}} diameter, [[sphere|spherical]] in shape with a rough surface. It matures in about 12 months, in autumn, at the same time as the next flowering. It is edible; the fruit is sweet when reddish. Seeds are small, brown and angular and are often [[seed dispersal|dispersed]] by [[frugivorous]] birds.{{cite journal|last1=Molina|first1=M.|last2=Pardo-De-Santayana|first2=M.|last3=Aceituno|first3=L. |last4=Morales |first4=R.|last5=Tardio|first5=J.|title=Fruit production of strawberry tree (Arbutus unedo L.) in two Spanish forests|journal=Forestry|date=1 October 2011|volume=84 |issue=4|pages=419–429|doi=10.1093/forestry/cpr031|issn=0015-752X|quote=Many frugivorous birds and several mammals feed on its fleshy fruits|doi-access=free}} The name '''''unedo''''' is attributed to [[Pliny the Elder]], who allegedly claimed that "''unum tantum edo''", meaning "I eat only one".{{cite wikisource |title=Naturalis Historia|wslink=Naturalis_Historia/Liber_XV#XXVIII||wslanguage=la|last=Gaius Plinius Secundus |authorlink=Pliny the Elder |date= |publisher= |location= |at=Liber XV. XXVIII, 99 |scan=}}
{{cite wikisource |title=Natural History |wslink= Natural History (Rackham, Jones, & Eichholz)/Book 15|last=Pliny The Elder |authorlink=Pliny the Elder |date= |publisher= |location= |volume= XV|at=XXVIII, 99 |scan=}} It is not known whether he meant that the fruit was so good he could eat only one, or whether he meant that the fruit was uninteresting so he ate only one.{{cite web|url=https://www.eattheweeds.com/the-strawberry-tree-curse-2/|title=Strawberry Tree Curse |website=Eat The Weeds and other things, too|date=31 August 2011}} ==Distribution== ''Arbutus unedo'' is widespread in the Mediterranean region: in [[Portugal]], [[Spain]], and southeastern [[France]]; southward in [[Algeria]], [[Morocco]], [[Libya]], and [[Tunisia]], and eastward in [[Italy]], [[Malta]], [[Slovenia]], [[Croatia]], [[Montenegro]], [[Greece]], [[Turkey]], [[Israel]], [[Palestine (region)|Palestine]], [[Jordan]], [[Lebanon]], and [[Syria]]. It is also found in western France, [[Albania]], [[Bulgaria]], and southwestern [[Ireland]].{{GRIN | access-date = 11 December 2017}} ''A. unedo'' has been noted for its [[disjunct distribution]], with isolated relict populations in southern and western Ireland in addition to its Mediterranean range. It is commonly cited as an example of the [[Lusitanian flora]], a small assemblage of plants native to Iberia and South-Western Ireland, but generally absent from Britain. Recent genetic studies have suggested that ''A. unedo'' may not be truly native in Ireland, but a Chalcolithic introduction.{{Cite journal|url=https://britishandirishbotany.org/index.php/bib/article/view/104|title=Is the Strawberry Tree, Arbutus unedo (Ericaceae), native to Ireland, or was it brought by the first copper miners?|first1=Micheline |last1=Sheehy Skeffington|first2=Nick|last2=Scott|date=30 December 2021|journal=British & Irish Botany|volume=3|issue=4|via=britishandirishbotany.org|doi=10.33928/bib.2021.03.385|doi-access=free}} The red-flowered variant, named ''A. unedo rubra'' by [[William Aiton]] in 1785, was discovered growing wild in Ireland in 1835.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}} ==Cultivation== ''Arbutus unedo'' is quite an easy plant to cultivate, and is adaptable to many climates. Once established it is fairly drought resistant, frost resistant, shade tolerant and [[Halotolerance|salt tolerant]].{{cite web|last1=Richins Myers|first1=Vanessa|title=Strawberry tree-Arbutus unedo|url=https://www.thespruce.com/strawberry-tree-arbutus-unedo-3269240|website=The Spruce|access-date=17 September 2017|quote=As long as you have made sure that it has regular watering for the first year so that the tree can form a strong root, it will be drought resistant. It can also grow in salty areas.}} Lower production of fruit mass has however been reported in case of summer droughts, and frosts in flowering time were seen to decrease the numbers of fruits.{{cite journal|last1=Molina|first1=María|last2=Pardo-De-Santayana|first2=Manuel|last3=Aceituno|first3=Laura|last4=Morales|first4=Ramón|last5=Tardío|first5=Javier|title=Fruit production of strawberry tree (Arbutus unedo L.) in two Spanish forests|journal=Forestry|date=1 October 2011|volume=84|issue=4|pages=419–429|doi=10.1093/forestry/cpr031|issn=0015-752X|quote=The number of fruits per branch appeared to be affected by frost risk at flowering time. [...] The number of fruits per branch appeared to be affected by frost risk at flowering time. |doi-access=free}} ''Arbutus unedo'' is naturally adapted to dry summer climates, and has become a very popular ornamental plant in California and the rest of the west coast of North America. It can grow easily in [[USDA hardiness zone]] 7 or warmer.{{cite web|title=Arbutus unedo - L.|url=https://pfaf.org/user/plant.aspx?latinname=Arbutus+unedo|publisher=Plants For a Future|access-date=17 September 2017}} It also grows well in the cool, wet summers of western Ireland and England, and temperate regions of Europe and Asia. Pests include [[scale insect|scales]] and [[thrips]], and diseases include [[anthracnose]], ''[[Phytophthora]]'', root rot, and [[Rust (fungus)|rust]].{{Citation needed|date=September 2017|}} Unlike most of the Ericaceae, ''A. unedo'' grows well in [[Base (chemistry)|basic]] (limy) [[Soil pH|pH soil]]s, even though it does better in more acidic soils. The fruit production is not very high and is highly variable on the weather, and that may be part of the reason this plant is not frequently cultivated. The average yield in a two years study is around 46 [[kg]] per [[hectare]], and 180 grams per cubic metre of crown.{{cite journal|last1=Molina|first1=María|last2=Pardo-De-Santayana|first2=Manuel|last3=Aceituno|first3=Laura|last4=Morales|first4=Ramón|last5=Tardío|first5=Javier|title=Fruit production of strawberry tree (Arbutus unedo L.) in two Spanish forests|journal=Forestry|date=1 October 2011|volume=84|issue=4|pages=419–429, tables 1–4|doi=10.1093/forestry/cpr031|issn=0015-752X|doi-access=free}} However, very little work has so far been done in terms of genotype selection.{{cite journal|last1=Celikel|first1=Gulay|last2=Demirsoy|first2=Leyla|last3=Demirsoy|first3=Husnu|title=The strawberry tree (Arbutus unedo L.) selection in Turkey|journal=Scientia Horticulturae|date=16 September 2008|volume=118|issue=2|pages=115–119|doi=10.1016/j.scienta.2008.05.028|bibcode=2008ScHor.118..115C }} ''Arbutus unedo'' has been seen to form a [[mycorrhiza]]l relationship. Inoculation with ''[[Pisolithus tinctorius]]'' has shown to greatly improve the plant's root mass, size, tolerance to drought and nutritional status.{{cite journal|last1=Navarro|first1=A.|last2=Sánchez-Blanco|first2=M. J.|last3=Morte|first3=A.|last4=Bañón|first4=S.|title=The influence of mycorrhizal inoculation and paclobutrazol on water and nutritional status of Arbutus unedo L.|journal=Environmental and Experimental Botany|date=1 September 2009|volume=66|issue=3|pages=362–371|doi=10.1016/j.envexpbot.2009.04.005|bibcode=2009EnvEB..66..362N }}{{cite journal|last1=Navarro García|first1=Alejandra|last2=Del Pilar Bañón Árias|first2=Sebastián|last3=Morte|first3=Asunción|last4=Sánchez-Blanco|first4=María Jesús|title=Effects of nursery preconditioning through mycorrhizal inoculation and drought in Arbutus unedo L. plants|journal=Mycorrhiza|date=2010|volume=21|issue=1|pages=53–64|doi=10.1007/s00572-010-0310-x| pmid = 20405149|s2cid=20470083|issn=1432-1890}} In cultivation in the UK, the [[Form (botany)|form]] ''A. unedo'' f. ''rubra''{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/94930/i-Arbutus-unedo-i-f-i-rubra-i/Details | title = ''Arbutus unedo'' f. ''rubra'' | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 13 January 2018}} and the [[cultivar]] 'Atlantic'{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/153810/i-Arbutus-unedo-i-Atlantic/Details |title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Arbutus unedo'' 'Atlantic' | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date=12 January 2018}} have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]. ===Propagation=== [[Plant propagation|Propagation]] can be done via [[seed]],{{Cite journal|last1=Bertsouklis|first1=Konstantinos F.|last2=Papafotiou|first2=Maria|date=2013-03-01|title=Seed Germination of Arbutus unedo, A. andrachne and Their Natural Hybrid A. andrachnoides in Relation to Temperature and Period of Storage|url=https://journals.ashs.org/hortsci/view/journals/hortsci/48/3/article-p347.xml|journal=HortScience|volume=48|issue=3|pages=347–351|doi=10.21273/HORTSCI.48.3.347|issn=0018-5345|doi-access=free}} [[layering (horticulture)|layering]], or [[cutting (plant)|cutting]]. The seed should undergo a one-month [[Stratification (seeds)#Cold stratification|cold stratification]] period,{{cite journal |last1=Pipinis |first1=Elias |title=Effects of Cold Stratification and Ga3 on Germination Ofarbutus Unedoseeds of Three Provenances |last2=Stampoulidis |first2=Athanasios |last3=Milios|first3=Elias |last4=Kitikidou|first4=Kyriaki |last5=Radoglou|first5=Kalliopi|journal=African Journal of Traditional, Complementary and Alternative Medicines |date=2017 |volume=14 |issue=1|pages=318–323|doi=10.21010/ajtcam.v14i1.34| pmid = 28480410 |issn=2505-0044|quote=in all three provenances seed germinability was significantly improved by a one-month period of CS or treatment |pmc=5411884}} then soaked for 5 to 6 days in warm water to improve germination success. Seedlings are prone to damp, and should be cared for in the first year. Germination rate is low, rarely over 20%.{{cite journal|last1=Hammami|first1=I.|last2=Jellal|first2=M.|last3=Ksontini|first3=M.|last4=Rejeb|first4=M.N.|title=Propagation of the Strawberry Tree Through Seed (Arbutus unedo)|journal=International Journal of Agriculture & Biology|date=2005|volume=7|pages=457–459|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/229694726|access-date=17 September 2017|quote=In the case of A. unedo, most prior studies found very low germination percentages, varying between 0 and 5 % (Smiris et al. 2006: 0 %; Demirsoy et al. 2010:1–3 %; Tilki 2004: 4 %; Ertekın and Kırdar 2010: 5 %). Hammami et al. (2005), however, obtained a considerably better result (19 %).}} Layering can take up to two years, but has a good success rate, while cutting is done with a {{convert|15-20|cm|in|frac=2|abbr=on}} long mature wood, preferably with a heel in November to December. The success rate however is not very high.{{cite web|title=Arbutus unedo, The Strawberry Tree|url=https://pfaf.org/user/cmspage.aspx?pageid=55 |publisher=Plants For a Future}} ==Uses== ===Culinary uses=== [[File:Arbutus unedo crumble cake.jpg|left|thumb|Crumble cake]] Arbutus berries have a high content of [[sugars]] (40%), and [[antioxidant]] vitamins{{Cite journal |last1=Bertsouklis |first1=Konstantinos F. |last2=Daskalakis |first2=Ioannis |last3=Biniari |first3=Katerina |last4=Papafotiou |first4=Maria |date=2021-02-15 |title=Comparative study of polyphenolic content and antioxidant capacity in fruits of Arbutus unedo, A. andrachne and their natural hybrid A.× andrachnoides |url=https://www.notulaebotanicae.ro/index.php/nbha/article/view/12165 |journal=Notulae Botanicae Horti Agrobotanici Cluj-Napoca |volume=49 |issue=1 |article-number=12165 |doi=10.15835/nbha49112165 |issn=1842-4309 |s2cid=233932055 |doi-access=free}} such as [[vitamin C|vitamin'' ''C]], [[beta-carotene]], [[Niacin (nutrient)|niacin]], [[tocopherols]], and organic acids that are precursors to [[omega-3]] and [[omega-6 fatty acid]]s (nearly 9%).{{cite journal|last1=Alarcão-E-Silva|first1=M. L. C. M. M.|last2=Leitão|first2=A. E. B.|last3=Azinheira|first3=H. G.|last4=Leitão|first4=M. C. A.|title=The Arbutus Berry: Studies on its Color and Chemical Characteristics at Two Mature Stages|journal=Journal of Food Composition and Analysis|date=1 February 2001|volume=14|issue=1|pages=27–35 |doi=10.1006/jfca.2000.0962|quote=Arbutus berry appears to be a good source of vitamins, namely niacin, ascorbic acid and β -carotene (content of 9.1, 346.3 and 70.9 mg/100 g, respectively), organic acids (nearly 9%), total sugars (c. 42%) and tannins (1.75 mg g−1).}}{{cite journal|last1=Barros|first1=Lillian|last2=Carvalho|first2=Ana Maria|last3=Morais|first3=Jorge Sá|last4=Ferreira|first4=Isabel C. F. R.|title=Strawberry-tree, blackthorn and rose fruits: Detailed characterisation in nutrients and phytochemicals with antioxidant properties|journal=Food Chemistry|date=1 May 2010|volume=120|issue=1|pages=247–254|doi=10.1016/j.foodchem.2009.10.016|quote=The analysed fruits contain very useful bioactive phytochemicals such as phenolics, vitamins (ascorbic acid and tocopherols) and carotenoids [..] The combination of bioactive compounds and rich nutritional composition (high contents in carbohydrates, low contents in fat with the precious contribution of polyunsaturated fatty acids, precursors of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids) of the studied wild fruits make them a very special food.|hdl=10198/2713|hdl-access=free}} They are edible fresh, but seldom consumed in that state - not least because the mature fruit tends to bruise very easily, making transportation difficult. They are used mostly for jam, marmalades, yogurt and [[alcoholic beverages]],{{cite journal|last1=Bonet|first1=M. Angels|last2=Vallès|first2=Joan|title=Use of non-crop food vascular plants in Montseny biosphere reserve (Catalonia, Iberian Peninsula)|journal=International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition|date=2002|volume=53 |issue=3 |pages=225–248|issn=0963-7486|pmid=11951586|doi=10.1080/09637480220132841|s2cid=30114836}} such as the Portuguese ''[[medronho]]'', a type of strong brandy. Many regions of [[Albania]] prepare the traditional drink [[rakia]] from the fruits of the plant ({{Lang|sq|mare}} or {{Lang|sq|kocimare}} in [[Albanian language|Albanian]]), whence comes the name of the drink, which is ''raki kocimarje''. The flowers are pollinated by [[apis mellifera|bees]], and the resulting [[honey]] is bitter tasting but still considered a delicacy.{{cite journal |title= Floral markers of strawberry tree (Arbutus unedo L.) honey| pmid=19919097 | doi=10.1021/jf9024147 | volume=58 | issue=1 | journal=J Agric Food Chem | pages=384–9 | last1 = Tuberoso | first1 = CI | last2 = Bifulco | first2 = E | last3 = Caboni | first3 = P | last4 = Cottiglia | first4 = F | last5 = Cabras | first5 = P | last6 = Floris | first6 = I| year=2010 | bibcode=2010JAFC...58..384T }} ===Herbal medicine=== ''Arbutus unedo'''s leaves have been employed in traditional and [[folk medicine]] in the form of [[decoction|a decoction]] said to have the following properties: astringent, diuretic, urinary anti-septic, antiseptic, intoxicant, rheumatism, tonic, and more recently, in the therapy of hypertension and diabetes.{{cite journal|last1=Mariotto|first1=S.|last2=Ciampa|first2=A. R.|last3=de Prati|first3=A. Carcereri|last4=Darra|first4=E.|last5=Vincenzi|first5=S. |last6=Sega|first6=M. |last7=Cavalieri|first7=E.|last8=Shoji|first8=K.|last9=Suzuki|first9=H.|title=Aqueous extract of Arbutus unedo inhibits STAT1 activation in human breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231 and human fibroblasts through SHP2 activation|journal=Medicinal Chemistry|date=2008|volume=4|issue=3|pages=219–228| pmid = 18473914|issn=1573-4064 |doi=10.2174/157340608784325179}}[https://web.archive.org/web/20080923212629/http://www.ars-grin.gov/cgi-bin/duke/ethnobot.pl?Arbutus%20unedo Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases: Ethnobotanical uses of ''Arbutus unedo'']. The leaves are reported to have a high concentration of [[flavonols|flavonol]] antioxidants, especially [[quercetin]], best extracted with a decoction, and together with the fruits are a source of antioxidants.{{cite journal|author1=Ioannis Erkekoglou|author2=Nikolaos Nenadis|author3=Efrosini Samara|author4=Fani Th. Mantzouridou|title=Functional Teas from the Leaves of Arbutus unedo: Phenolic Content, Antioxidant Activity, and Detection of Efficient Radical Scavengers|journal=Plant Foods for Human Nutrition|date=June 2017|volume=72|issue=2|pages=176–183|pmid=28421300|doi=10.1007/s11130-017-0607-4|s2cid=403426}}{{cite journal|last1=Mendes|first1=Lídia|last2=de Freitas|first2=Victor|last3=Baptista|first3=Paula|last4=Carvalho|first4=Márcia|title=Comparative antihemolytic and radical scavenging activities of strawberry tree (Arbutus unedo L.) leaf and fruit|journal=Food and Chemical Toxicology |date=2011|volume=49|issue=9|pages=2285–2291|doi=10.1016/j.fct.2011.06.028|pmid = 21703325|issn=1873-6351}} The nectar contains the isoprenoid unedone (2-(1,2-dihydroxypropyl)-4,4,8-trimethyl-1-oxaspiro[2.5]oct-7-en-6-one) which is biologically active against a common and debilitating parasite of bumble bees, ''[[Crithidia bombi]]'', so could provide a naturally occurring way for bees to withstand the burden of disease which has been reported to be a contributing factor in pollinator declines. The compound is glycosylated to an inactive form unedone-8-O-glycoside once consumed by the bee (perhaps to reduce any toxic effects against the bee) then transformed back to the active aglycone by the bee's microbiome in the hindgut where the parasite is most prevalent and damaging - suggesting that the microbiome assists in the anti-parasitic process.{{cite journal |author1=Koch, H |author2=Welcome, V|author3=Kendal-Smith, A |author4=Thursfield, L |author5=Farrell, IW |author6= Langat, MK |author7=Brown, MJF |author8=Stevenson, PC |title=Host and gut microbiome modulate the antiparasitic activity of nectar metabolites in a bumblebee pollinator |journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B |date=2022 |volume=377 |issue=1853 |page=20210164 |doi=10.1098/rstb.2021.0162|pmid=35491601 |pmc=9058528 }} === Ecological design === In [[landscape design]], [[ecosystem restoration]] or [[permaculture]] based designs, ''A. unedo'' can have many purposes. While the ornamental one is the most common, this can be a valuable plant also for restoring degraded ecosystems and preventing [[desertification]]. Being a pioneer plant and growing well also in poor soils, it can be used in a wide array of situations. * The [[flowers]] are a significant source of nectar and pollen for bees, while the fruits are food for the birds. * Its salt tolerance, coupled with it being an [[evergreen]], make it a good choice for wind barriers in lands close to the sea. * ''A. unedo'' is [[Fire ecology#Fire resistance|fire resistant]] (can regrow after a fire), and being a pioneer plant can contribute to the discontinuity of fire-prone pines and eucalyptus monocultures;{{cite book|author1=Maria Filomena Figueiredo Nazaré Gomes|title=Strategies for the improvement of Arbutus unedo L. (strawberry tree): in vitro propagation, mycorrhization and diversity analysis|date=2011|publisher=Departamento de Ciências da Vida Universidade de Coimbra|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/278004210 |access-date=July 30, 2020|quote=A. unedo may contribute to the discontinuity of the forest biomass due to monocultures of pines and eucalyptus, particularly in the centre and north regions of Portugal, a situation responsible for the high number of fires and high fire intensity that all summers occur in these areas of the country}} for the same reasons it is a good candidate for reforestation in Mediterranean areas.{{cite book|author1=Maria Filomena Figueiredo Nazaré Gomes|title=Strategies for the improvement of Arbutus unedo L. (strawberry tree): in vitro propagation, mycorrhization and diversity analysis|date=2011|publisher=Departamento de Ciências da Vida Universidade de Coimbra|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/278004210|access-date=July 30, 2020|quote=The species is drought tolerant and able to regenerate following forestry fires making it quite interesting for forestation programs in Mediterranean regions.}} * The dense foliage throughout the year can be a shelter for insects and small animals during the [[winter]]. * Its extensive [[root system]] can help in the soil stabilization process.{{cite book|author1=Maria Filomena Figueiredo Nazaré Gomes|title=Strategies for the improvement of Arbutus unedo L. (strawberry tree): in vitro propagation, mycorrhization and diversity analysis|date=2011|publisher=Departamento de Ciências da Vida Universidade de Coimbra|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/19131968.pdf|access-date=19 September 2017|quote=[A. unedo] contributes to maintain biodiversity, helps to stabilize soils and survives well in marginal lands}} ===Other uses=== * The wood is quite hard and well suited for a various uses such as [[fire wood]] and to make [[Smoking pipe|pipes]]. Since it does not usually grow straight, it is not well suited for construction or similar uses. * The tree is also grown as an ornamental plant, because of its nice-looking and -smelling flowers and fruit and their interesting presence on the plant at the same time, and because it is an evergreen. It is used as a single or multi-trunked [[ornamental tree]], and as a specimen or [[hedge]] [[shrub]] in gardens and public landscapes. == History == [[File:Badaia - Barranco de los Goros - Madroño 04.jpg|thumb|right|upright|alt=Tree|Wild specimens in fruit, Spain]] [[File:Arbutus unedo fruiting in Dunbar 1.jpg|thumb|Cultivated specimen fruiting profusely in a Scottish garden]] Its Mediterranean habitat, elegant details of leaf and habit and dramatic show of fruit with flowers made ''Arbutus unedo'' notable in [[Classical Antiquity]], when it was called Andrachne, and for which Theophrastos (4th c. BCE) wrote about it, as well as the ancient army medical herbalist Pedanios Dioscorides [De Materia Medica, Book II-150]; in addition, [[Pliny the Elder|Pliny]] thought it should not be planted where bees are kept, for the bitterness it imparts to honey.{{Citation needed|date=February 2021}} The first evidence of its importation into northern European gardens was to 16th-century England from Ireland. In 1586 a correspondent in Ireland sent plants to the Elizabethan courtiers [[Robert Dudley, 1st Earl of Leicester|Lord Leicester]] and [[Sir Francis Walsingham]].Quoted in Alice M. Coats, ''Garden Shrubs and Their Histories'' (1964) 1992, ''s.v.'' "Arbutus". An earlier description by [[William Turner (naturalist)|Rev. William Turner]] (''The Names of Herbes'', 1548) was probably based on hearsay. The Irish association of ''Arbutus'' in English gardens is reflected in the inventory taken in 1649 of [[Henrietta Maria of France|Henrietta Maria]]'s [[Wimbledon, London#17th century|Wimbledon]]: "one very fayre tree, called the Irish arbutis standing in the midle parte of the sayd kitchin garden, very lovely to look upon" By the 18th century ''Arbutus unedo'' was well known enough in English gardens for [[Batty Langley]] to make the bold and impractical suggestion that it might be used for hedges, though it "will not admit of being clipped as other evergreens are". In the United States, [[Thomas Jefferson]] lists the plant in his [[Monticello]] gardens in 1778.Ann Leighton, ''American Gardens in the Eighteenth Century: 'For Use or Delight' '', 1976:395. The form ''A. unedo'' f. ''rubra''{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Arbutus unedo'' f. ''rubra''|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=159|access-date=30 May 2013}} and the hybrid ''A. ''× ''andrachnoides'',{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Arbutus x andrachnoides''|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=160|access-date=30 May 2013}} have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]. ==Symbolic uses== ===Ancient history=== [[Image: Sirolo-vista_conero.jpg|thumb|right|[[Mount Conero]], Italy, whose name is derived from [[Greek language|Greek]] {{lang|el|κόμαρος}} ({{transliteration|el|komaròs}}) and indicates the strawberry tree which is common on the slopes of the mountain]] The tree is mentioned by Roman poet [[Ovid]], in Book I: 89–112 "The Golden Age" of his ''[[Metamorphoses]]'': "Contented with food that grew without cultivation, they collected mountain strawberries and the fruit of the strawberry tree, wild cherries, blackberries clinging to the tough brambles, and acorns fallen from Jupiter's spreading oak-tree."{{cite book|url=http://www.poetryintranslation.com/PITBR/Latin/Metamorph.htm |title=The Metamorphoses |volume= Book I |author=Ovid |translator=A. S. Kline|website=Poetry in Translation|access-date=7 December 2022}} In his ''[[Description of Greece]]'', [[Pausanias (geographer)|Pausanias]] associated the tree with the god [[Hermes]].{{Cite web |title=Pausanias, Description of Greece, 9.22.2 |url=https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Paus.+9.22&fromdoc=Perseus%3Atext%3A1999.01.0160 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211126093229/http://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Paus.+9.22&fromdoc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0160 |archive-date=26 November 2021 |access-date=20 February 2021}} The name of the Italian promontory [[Mount Conero]], situated directly south of the port of [[Ancona]] on the [[Adriatic Sea]], derives from the Greek name κόμαρος (komaròs) indicating the strawberry tree which is common on the slopes of the mountain.S. Pignatti, ''Flora d'Italia'', volume II, p. 261, Edagricole, 1982. {{ISBN|9788820623128}} Mount Conero, the only coastal high point on the Adriatic sea between [[Trieste]] and the [[Gargano]] massif in the region of [[Apulia]], has assisted navigators in sailing across the Adriatic sea since ancient times.Braccesi L., & Luni M. (Eds.). I greci in Adriatico, 2 (Hesperìa, Vol. 18). L'Erma Di Bretschneider, 2004, p.54 {{ISBN|8882652661}}. ===Italy=== The strawberry tree ({{Langx|it|corbezzolo}} {{IPA|it|korˈbettsolo|}}) began to be considered one of the [[national symbols of Italy]] in the 19th century, during the [[Italian unification]], because with its autumn colors is reminiscent of the [[flag of Italy]] (green for its leaves, white for its flowers and red for its berries).{{in lang|it}} various authors - Guida pratica agli alberi e arbusti in Italia; Biblioteca per chi ama la natura - Selezione dal Reader's Digest Milano 1983, 1991. For this reason the poet [[Giovanni Pascoli]] dedicated a poem to the strawberry tree. He refers to the [[Aeneid]] passage in which [[Pallas (son of Evander)|Pallas]], killed by [[Turnus]], was posed on branches of a strawberry tree. He saw in the colours of that plant a prefiguration of the [[flag of Italy]] and considered Pallas the first ''national cause martyr''.Giovanni Pascoli, in the autograph note to his poem "Il corbezzolo" ("The strawberry tree"), compared the [[virgil]]ian, deposed after death on branches of a strawberry tree, to the Italian martyrs wrapped up, during the burial ceremonies, in the Italian flag. Pascoli's ode says: [[File:Giovanni Pascoli 01.jpg|thumb|[[Giovanni Pascoli]], an emblematic figure of [[Italian literature]] in the late 19th century.{{cite news |title=Giovanni Pascoll, Poet, Dead. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1912/04/07/archives/giovanni-pascoll-poet-dead.html |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=7 April 1912 |page=15}} Alongside [[Gabriele D'Annunzio]], he was one of the greatest Italian [[decadentism|decadent]] poets.]] {{Div col|colwidth=30em}} {{in lang|it}} {{blockquote|O verde albero italico, il tuo maggio
è nella bruma: s'anche tutto muora,
tu il giovanile gonfalon selvaggio
spieghi alla bora|author=Giovanni Pascoli}}
{{blockquote|Oh green Italian tree, your
May month
is in the mist: if everything
dies,
you, the youthful wild banner
unfold to the northern wind}} {{div col end}} {{Multiple image | align = right | image1 = Hieronymus Bosch - The Garden of Earthly Delights - Garden of Earthly Delights (Ecclesia's Paradise).jpg | width1 = 180 | caption1 = Central panel of ''[[The Garden of Earthly Delights]]'' by [[Hieronymus Bosch]], described by [[José de Sigüenza]] as "The Picture of the Strawberry Tree" | image2 = Escudo de Madrid.svg | width2 = 132 | caption2 = A bear and a ''madroño'' (strawberry tree) are the symbol of [[Coat of arms of Madrid|Madrid]]. }} ===Spain=== ''[[The Garden of Earthly Delights]]'', a painting by [[Hieronymus Bosch]], was originally listed by [[José de Sigüenza]], in the inventory of [[Philip II of Spain|the Spanish Crown]] as ''La Pintura del Madroño'' – "The Painting of the Strawberry Tree".Warner, Marion. [https://books.google.com/books?id=ng934k3IpRQC&pg=PA70 Fantastic metamorphoses, other worlds: ways of telling the self]. Oxford University Press, 2002. 70. The tree makes up part of the [[Coat of arms of Madrid]] ({{Lang|es|El oso y el madroño}}, The Bear and the Strawberry Tree) of the city of [[Madrid]], [[Spain]]. In the center of the city ([[Puerta del Sol]]) there is a [[Statue of the Bear and the Strawberry Tree|statue of a bear]] eating the fruit of the ''Madroño'' tree. The image appears on city crests, taxi cabs, man-hole covers, and other city infrastructure. The fruit of the ''Madroño'' tree ferments on the tree if left to ripen, so some of the bears become drunk from eating the fruits.{{Citation needed|date=June 2011}} {{clear}} ===Ireland=== "My love's an arbutus" is the title of a poem by the Irish writer [[Alfred Perceval Graves]] (1846–1931), set to music by his compatriot [[Charles Villiers Stanford]] (1852–1924).{{cite book|title=The New National Songbook |year=1906 |editor-first1=Charles Villiers |editor-last=Stanford |editor-first2=Geoffrey |editor-last2=Shaw}} Cited in the folkinfo.org song database, available
